R9644.summary: Hurtado's running account of Adrian VI: the Pope's good will but unsatisfying deeds, his parsimony while he waits for the archbishop of Bari, the payment of the papal household before the other side buys it, the French King's request for a safe-conduct for an ambassador, and a leak of letters shown in copy in Castile.

R9650.summary: The French are resolved to come into Italy and send a great sum of money to Lyon; Hieronymo Adorno has intercepted letters; the Pope, urged to act, answers lukewarmly and will not declare himself.
R9650.en:
Yesterday a post came from the Archbishop of Bari; he writes to me from the [23rd] to the [1st] of this month. He says
that within six days he would send one of his men here, by whom he would give full news; he says he would then send
another to Your Majesty. For this reason I do not send my letter to Your Majesty.

In substance he tells me that the French are resolved to come into Italy, and are sending a great sum of money to
Lyon, and that it is necessary to see to the defence, and that the Pope should do what he can, since more is at
stake for him than for anyone.

And I have told His Holiness that this warning has come to me from Hieronymo Adorno, from some letters he has
taken out of love for Your Majesty; and, for what he owes, let him not set himself against this;

R9652.summary: A letter entirely in clear: the licenciado Bernardino, a 'gran bellaco', has turned up in Rome and Adrian VI declines a night arrest in the city; the viceroy of Naples' news of the siege of Rhodes is forwarded in copy.
R9652.en:
I wrote to Your Majesty on the [x] of this month how the licentiate Bernardino had come here. Then I went to the
Duke, and spoke to His Holiness, and he told me he would order justice to be done on him, because he was a great
scoundrel.

The Duke came back here at once; he begged His Holiness to be pleased to let him have him arrested. The Pope answered
him that, if he was inside Rome, he would order it to be done, and if he was outside, that he should do as seemed good
to him. The Duke has learned that he is in the city, in his brother's house; he has sent to beg His Holiness to be
pleased that he may have him arrested there one night. The Pope has answered me that here it would not be well, but
that we should put in a petition that His Holiness order justice to be done.

Let Your Majesty write to the Duke what is to be done in this;

R9634.summary: Four months after the imperial sack of Genoa, Hurtado reports a plan put to him by Geronimo Adorno: the Emperor and the King of England should make war on the King of France through Provence, his weakest land, with six hundred men-at-arms, light horse and soldiers at 70,000 ducats a month, settled now for March; an early form of the 1524 Provence invasion.

R9646.summary: Adrian VI has concluded his settlement with Alfonso d'Este, duke of Ferrara, and a copy of the capitulation is being sent; Charles's request meets papal caution, and the archbishop [of Bari] advises an offer of money for the Pope's needs.

R9649.summary: Adrian VI asks Charles V to write urging him to garrison Ostia and give the fortress to no one, since Cardinal Santa Cruz (Carvajal) presses for it by seniority; the licenciado Bernardino has landed from Barcelona and hides at his brother's house. The cipher runs are deciphered and aligned with the contemporary clear version on f. 268.
R9649.en:
His Beatitude has commanded me to write to Your Majesty on his behalf that the Cardinal of Santa Cruz is pressing
him to death over Ostia, [claiming it] as he needs it, being the most senior in the College; [and] that he would
like Your Majesty to write to His Holiness that he should order a strong guard put in the fortress of Ostia, and
not give it to anyone, because he would not want to give it to him, nor to have him aggrieved.

At this moment I have learned that the licentiate Bernardino has come here; he embarked at Barcelona on the 5th
of last month. They tell me he is hidden in the house of a brother of his. I am informing the Duke at once, to see
what he thinks. Let Your Majesty write what you command. May Our Lord keep and increase Your Majesty's most royal
person and estate. From Rome, the 9th of November [1522].

R9645.summary: The terms of Adrian VI's capitulation with Alfonso d'Este, duke of Ferrara (the feudal dues, service to the Church, no confederation except with the Pope and the Emperor, no harbouring of disservants), then news of the duke's men and the Pope; f. 243r has no gloss and the reading rests on the key.

R9656.summary: The archbishop of Bari wrote no certain news of the coming of the French; the Pope will not fail the Emperor and is content for peace, but is very suspicious that Don Juan [Manuel] was ordered from there to do what he has done. A faded contemporary clear copy on f. 335r supports part of the reading.

system: Three-letter consonant-vowel-consonant nomenclator codes mixed inline with clear Spanish, with homophones at code level (ta and tu both = 'no'), codes used for syllables as well as whole words, and long words spelled letter by letter between the codes.
